intro: Freelance journalists get paid through invoices submitted to editors after project completion. This process often involves long wait times and inconsistent cash flow, making financial management a core part of your work.

Track every expense using dedicated Mac tools.

blocks.text: Why freelance financial management is a struggle

The financial struggle for freelance journalists is often systemic rather than a personal failure. You are essentially running a small business while trying to report the news. This requires you to act as your own accountant, manager, and IT support. These administrative tasks consume hours that you could spend on actual reporting.

Inconsistent cash flow is another major hurdle. Your income might swing wildly between months. This makes it difficult to manage standard obligations like rent or car payments. Unlike staff reporters, you lack institutional support for legal, safety, or basic benefits. You pay for these out of pocket.
How to manage money as a freelance journalist on your Mac

items: Open a dedicated business checking account. Never mix business income with personal spending.
Use a dedicated business credit card for all your work-related expenses.
Implement cash flow smoothing. When a large payment arrives, keep it in your business account. Pay yourself a consistent salary each month to mimic a steady paycheck.
Map out all potential expenses before pitching. Include research hours, transport, and taxes to ensure your rate is worth the effort.
Join organizations like the National Writers Union. Use their rate sharing databases to negotiate better pay.

blocks.text: If you work for a media organization, always follow their specific rules regarding client data or sensitive financial documents. Keep your local files encrypted.

faq.question: How do I deal with late payments?
faq.answer: Send polite but firm reminders. Use a template to track when invoices were sent and when they are due. If you use an app like Invoice Rex, it can often automate these reminders for you.

faq.question: Should I use free or paid accounting software?
faq.answer: Start with free options like Wave or GnuCash. They offer enough functionality to track expenses and income without adding to your monthly overhead.

causes.title: Stagnant pay rates

fixes.title: Separate your accounts
fixes.text: Use a dedicated business account to keep personal and professional finances distinct.

fixes.title: Salary model
fixes.text: Pay yourself a consistent monthly salary from your business account to stabilize cash flow.
